tagline.en: Use a, an, the, in, on and at with confidence
tagline.bn: a, an, the, in, on, at ঠিকভাবে ব্যবহার করো

subtitle.en: Small words, big difference. Every card has a short rule and 3 questions: when to say a, an or the, and where in, on and at go.
subtitle.bn: ছোট শব্দ, কিন্তু অনেক গুরুত্বপূর্ণ। প্রতিটি কার্ডে ছোট্ট নিয়ম আর ৩টি প্রশ্ন: কখন a, an বা the, আর কোথায় in, on, at।

hint.en: a, an, the, or no article
hint.bn: a, an, the, নাকি কিছুই না

hint.en: Where something is, or where it goes

cards.badge: a + consonant sound · an + vowel sound

rule.en: Use “an” before a vowel sound (an apple, an hour) and “a” before a consonant sound (a book, a university). Listen to the sound, not the letter.
rule.bn: স্বরধ্বনির (vowel sound) আগে “an”, ব্যঞ্জনধ্বনির আগে “a”। অক্ষর নয়, উচ্চারণ শুনে ঠিক করো।

recap.example: an egg · an hour · a cat · a uniform

options.why: “Umbrella” starts with a vowel sound (“um”), so it needs an.
“Book” starts with a consonant sound, so it needs a.
“Orange” starts with a vowel sound, so it needs an.

questions.explanation: “Umbrella” starts with a vowel sound, so use an.

options.why: You don’t say the h in “hour”, so it sounds like “our”: an hour.
You do say the h in “horse”, so it is “a horse”.
You do say the h in “house”, so it is “a house”.

questions.explanation: The h in “hour” is silent, so it starts with a vowel sound: an hour.

options.why: “University” sounds like “yoo-niversity”, a consonant sound, so use a.
“Student” starts with a consonant sound: a student.
The h in “honest” is silent, so it is “an honest student”.

questions.explanation: “University” starts with a “yoo” sound, which is a consonant sound, so use a.

cards.badge: the + a thing we both know

rule.en: Use “the” when the listener knows which one you mean: you said it before, there is only one, or it is clear from the place.
rule.bn: শ্রোতা যখন জানে তুমি কোনটির কথা বলছ (আগে বলা হয়েছে, একটিই আছে, বা পরিস্থিতি থেকে বোঝা যায়) তখন “the”।

recap.example: I saw a dog. The dog was big. · The sun is hot.

questions.prompt: I bought a book. ___ book is about birds.

options.why: We already talked about this book, so we use the.
“An” is for a vowel sound, and the book is already known.
“Some” is for more than one, or for things you can’t count.

questions.explanation: We already said “a book”, so now it is “the book”.

options.why: There is only one sun, so it is “the sun”.
“Sun” starts with a consonant sound, and there is only one: the.
We don’t say “some sun is hot” about the one sun in the sky.

questions.explanation: There is only one sun, so use the.

options.why: “A door” means any door. You mean this room’s door: the.
“Door” starts with a consonant sound, and you mean one known door.
“Some” is for more than one thing.

questions.explanation: You both know which door (the one in this room), so use the.

cards.badge: no article: by bus · play football

rule.en: Don’t use an article with games and sports, languages, school subjects, meals, or “by” + transport.
rule.bn: খেলা, ভাষা, স্কুলের বিষয়, খাবারের বেলা (breakfast, lunch) আর “by” + যানবাহনের আগে article বসে না।

recap.example: We play cricket. She speaks Bangla. I go by bus.

questions.prompt: She goes to school by ___ bus.

options.why: We say “by bus”, with no article.
We say “by bus”, not “by the bus”.
We say “by bus”, with no article.

questions.explanation: After “by” with transport, we don’t use an article: by bus, by car.

options.why: Sports take no article: play football.
We say “play football”, not “play the football”.
Sports take no article.

questions.explanation: Sports and games don’t take an article: play football.

options.why: We say “speak English”, not “speak the English”.
Languages take no article.
Languages take no article.

questions.explanation: Languages don’t take an article: speak English.

cards.badge: at 5 pm · on Monday · in July

rule.en: Use “at” for clock times, “on” for days and dates, and “in” for months, years and seasons.
rule.bn: ঘড়ির সময়ে “at”, দিন ও তারিখে “on”, আর মাস, বছর ও ঋতুতে “in”।

recap.example: at 7 o’clock · on Friday · in 2026 · in winter

options.why: “On” is for days and dates, not clock times.
“In” is for months, years and seasons.
“To” shows direction, not a time.

questions.explanation: Clock times use at.

options.why: “At” is for clock times.
“In” is for months and years, not days.
“To” shows direction, not a day.

questions.explanation: Days of the week use on.

questions.prompt: We go to Cox’s Bazar ___ December.

options.why: “At” is for clock times.
“On” is for days and dates, like “on 5 December”.
“To” shows direction, not a month.

questions.explanation: Months use in.

rule.en: Use “for” with a length of time (for two hours). Use “since” with the moment something started (since Monday).
rule.bn: সময়ের দৈর্ঘ্য বোঝাতে “for” (for two hours); শুরুর মুহূর্ত বোঝাতে “since” (since Monday)।

questions.prompt: I have lived here ___ ten years.

options.why: “Since” needs a starting point, like “since 2016”.
We say “for ten years” with “have lived”.
“Ago” comes after the time (“ten years ago”) and goes with the simple past.

questions.explanation: “Ten years” is a length of time, so use for.

options.why: “For” needs a length of time, like “for three days”.
“Ago” goes after a length of time, with the simple past.
“At” is for clock times.

questions.explanation: “Monday” is when it started, so use since.

options.why: “Since” needs a starting point, not a length of time.
“Ago” would come after: “two hours ago”.
“At” is for a clock time, not how long.

questions.explanation: “Two hours” is a length of time: for.

cards.badge: at the door · on the desk · in the box

rule.en: Use “in” for inside something, “on” for touching a surface, and “at” for a point or place.
rule.bn: কোনো কিছুর ভেতরে থাকলে “in”, উপরিতল ছুঁয়ে থাকলে “on”, আর নির্দিষ্ট জায়গা বোঝাতে “at”।

recap.example: in the bag · on the wall · at the bus stop

options.why: “In” means inside. You can’t be inside a table.
“At the table” means sitting there, like people at dinner.
“To” shows movement, not where something is.

questions.explanation: The keys are lying on top of the table’s surface: on.

questions.prompt: The fish are swimming ___ the pond.

options.why: “On” means on top of the surface. The fish are inside the water.
“At” is a point, not inside something.
“To” shows movement towards a place.

questions.explanation: The fish are inside the water: in.

options.why: A person can’t be inside a door.
“On the door” is for things stuck to it, like a poster.
“To” shows movement, not where someone is.

questions.explanation: A person waiting by the door is at the door.

rule.en: “Under” is below. “Between” is in the middle of two things. “Next to” is beside. “Behind” is at the back of.
rule.bn: “Under” = নিচে, “between” = দুটির মাঝে, “next to” = পাশে, “behind” = পেছনে।

recap.example: The ball is under the chair. B is between A and C.

questions.prompt: The cat is sleeping ___ the bed.

options.why: “Between” needs two things, like “between the bed and the wall”.
We need “next to”, not just “next”.
“Among” is for a group of many things.

questions.explanation: Below the bed: under.

questions.prompt: The letter B is ___ A and C.

options.why: “Among” is for a group of three or more. Here there are two letters.
B is beside the letters, not below them.
B is in the middle, not at the back.

questions.explanation: In the middle of two things: between.

questions.prompt: Sit ___ me, so we can share the book.

options.why: “Between” needs two people or things.
You can’t share a book sitting under someone.
“Among” is for a group, not one person.

questions.explanation: Beside someone: next to.

cards.badge: go to · jump into · come from

rule.en: “To” shows where you are going. “Into” means going inside something. “From” shows where you started.
rule.bn: “To” = কোথায় যাচ্ছ, “into” = কোনো কিছুর ভেতরে ঢোকা, “from” = কোথা থেকে।

recap.example: Walk to the shop. Jump into the pool. A letter from Grandma.

options.why: “Into” means going inside. We say “go to school”.
“At” is for where you are, not where you go.
“In” is for inside, not for going somewhere.

questions.explanation: Going towards a place: to.

options.why: “To” shows direction, but the frog went inside the water: into.
“At” is a point, not movement inside.
“On” is the top of a surface. The frog went in.

questions.explanation: Moving from outside to inside: into.

options.why: “To” is where you go, not where you start.
“Into” means going inside something.
“At” is for where you are now.

questions.explanation: Where someone started or was born: from.
